newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal- Basis firm in eastern Corn Belt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal- Basis firm in eastern Corn Belt.

text.p: Soymeal basis levels were steady to higher on Thursday, with markets east of the Mississippi River particularly firm supported by strong export and domestic demand, soymeal brokers said.
"The southeast poultry market is consuming a lof of meal right now and export trade has been really significant," one Indiana-based cash source said.
The truck basis for 48 percent meal at Frankfort, Indiana rose $1.00 to $15 over December CBOT futures, while in Decatur, Indiana the truck basis was up $2.00 to $20 over Dec.
Heavy demand was seen keeping the crush pace strong.
Estimates for the weekly NOPA crush ranged from 28.2 million to 28.7 million bushels, compared with 27.89 million the previous week.
"We're crushing as hard as we ever have but there's not a whole lot (of soybeans) available and exports are sucking out everything we have," one broker said.
Delays to the harvest caused by wet weather in the U.S. Midwest were seen keeping soybean supplies tight east of the Mississippi River.
